gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-khula: Bushcraft spaces its letters wide and draws every curve without a weight shift. Khula's tall midsection and open curves make a sturdy sans counterpart, and that closed-versus-open split is the best thing about the pairing.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-krub: Krub reads as a plain sans with a pronounced x-height and curves that stop before the loop closes. Bushcraft's closed, widely spaced forms make a striking foil.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-kufam: Bushcraft stretches its letters wide, with capitals that barely rise above the lowercase. And Kufam, a plain sans drawn like neon tubing, makes the heading look quite shrunken if you ever make it small.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-lexend: Lexend comes in with oversized lowercase and open jaws on every curve, friendly and unhurried. Bushcraft feels artistic and wide-spaced beside it, closed where Lexend is open, like a sketch next to a clear sentence.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-lexend-deca: Wide-spaced letters with no weight shift in any curve give Bushcraft its expressive, artistic look. And Lexend Deca's unshaded line and big lowercase offer a clean, approachable sans that lets that closed heading stand out.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-liter: Extra-wide spacing and curves that never change width make Bushcraft instantly recognizable. Liter, a plain sans with zero stroke contrast and tall, open-mouthed lowercase, does the quiet work of carrying the text while Bushcraft handles the expression.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-mada: Artistic and a bit stubborn, Bushcraft keeps its line width through every turn and closes its shapes firmly. Mada's towering midzone and curves that refuse to close make it the perfect opposite.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-martel-sans: Bushcraft has a pen-plotter smoothness, with wide spacing and capitals that barely stand out from the lowercase. And Martel Sans, a plain sans with generous curve openings and a high mean line, gives the heading room to be bold.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-matangi: Twine on a flat surface, that is Matangi's hefty lowercase with its rounded letters left open, set under Bushcraft's closed, widely spaced forms. Use the heading big.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-maven-pro: Bushcraft is the expressive voice here, with wide spacing and a line that never changes weight. Maven Pro is the steady one, with a welcoming gap in the c and a high-waisted lowercase made for reading.
